newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's primary Cetes rates fall on bank easing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's primary Cetes rates fall on bank easing.

text.p: Mexico's primary Cetes rates fell more than expected on Tuesday after the central bank gave a signal earlier in the day that it was willing to allow easier monetary conditions, analysts said.
The rate on the bellwether one-month treasury bills fell 77 basis points to 29.08 percent, while longer-term rates also fell at Banco de Mexico's primary treasury bill auction.
The trigger for the sharp decline was the move by Banco de Mexico around noon on Tuesday to ease its daily liquidity objective for the money markets to zero from a minus 20 million pesos a day.
"From yesterday, most people were expecting rates to be stable. The move by the Banco de Mexico to ease was very important," said Santander Investment economist Hector Chavez.
Conditions were right for a small drop or for rates to be stable at the auction this week, with the peso increasingly stable and inflation more or less in line with expectations, analysts said.

But rates were pushed down more sharply across the yield curve after the central bank signalled it was happy with the stable peso and was ready to sanction the traditional sharp year-end demand for cash in Mexico.

"The fundamental reason for the change in expectations in the market in the last couple of hours of operation was the announcement from the central bank that it would modify its daily liquidity objective," said Ricardo Vazquez, an analyst with Banco Union.
"The peso's return to stability has encouraged the authorities to signal a desire for somewhat easier interest rates going forward," said market analysis group, IDEA.
Earlier on Tuesday, a Reuters survey of 10 Cetes dealers found expectations for a drop in the bellwether 28-day Cetes of 44 points to 29.41 percent, and a decline in longer term rates.
Before falling slightly at the primary auction last week rates had risen for five consecutive weeks as the central bank was seen sanctioning higher rates to help the exchange rate stabilise.
But the peso has stabilised recently.
On Tuesday, the benchmark 48-hour peso contract closed 1.1 centavos firmer at 7.8710/7.8760 per dollar.
At the auction this week, the rate on the three-month paper fell 176 basis points to 27.70 percent, while the six-month paper showed a decline of 70 basis points to 27.09 percent.
The yield on 343-day paper this week was 26.50 percent, compared with 26.74 percent on 350-day paper last week. -- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559
